title: Carbon 3D · High-Momentum Tolerance and Correlated-Fault Stress

partition.reusedKnownFailure: run 146514, event 147609488, pz1 3309.59 GeV; legacy tolerance 16.598 GeV

cases.rule: pz1+=5; eta1=asinh(pz1/pt1); makes angular consistency tautologically pass
as correlated case, then E1=sqrt(px1²+py1²+pz1²+m_mu²); can defeat both redundant consistency checks

methods.threshold: same capped angular threshold; energy witness |E1-sqrt(px1²+py1²+pz1²+m_mu²)|>0.5+0.001*abs(E1) GeV; negative combined mass² invalid
methods.guard: angle mismatch OR energy-shell residual OR mass invalid
methods.onAlarm: repair pz using eta only on angular mismatch and successful physical consistency; otherwise quarantine (no automatic guess)

scoring.indices: retrospective and prospective separately; primary prospective hash bucket 1
scoring.abstention: quarantine is not a valid repaired measurement

limitations: Even the prospective hash bucket comes from the same CERN 2010 educational CSV, not an independent experiment.
All artificial faults are injected on genuine records; there are no claims of actual faulty CERN detectors.
pt, eta, pz, E, px, py all derive from reconstructed track information and are not independently instrumented ALICE/ATLAS/CMS/LHCb measurements.
Coherent edits that preserve all available redundant relations can be undetectable from these fields; abstain rather than fabricate original state.
Predeclared thresholds may harm clean coverage and will be reported without posthoc tuning.
Stored M and clean mass are derived from the same physical kinematics; measured gains only demonstrate software error recovery.
